note: Item B fixed a real contradiction, not a cosmetic one: ProviderQuotaBlock.levelOf() graded colour from remainingPercent against hardcoded 25/5 cutoffs and ignored the user's configured high/critical thresholds, while the displayed number switched with showAsUsed. Risk is now graded once from used-percent against the configured thresholds, and the number and bar fill share the chosen semantics. Item D was audited and needed no change (reset info already appears exactly once per window, in the title row) — recorded so phase 2 does not re-audit. The RawSettings mirrors are Option<bool> with a FIELD-level serde default on purpose: the struct-level default would have produced Some(true) and made an explicitly stored false indistinguishable from an absent key.

operation: Closed both P1 findings from the independent phase-1 review. P1-1: removed the consumerless taskbar_reset_time_relative setting (rather than fabricating a consumer) and made re-adding it a compile error plus a test failure. P1-2: added the shared primaryQuotaState predicate and gated ProviderGrid on it so non-quota providers never render a percentage.
note: P1-1 was resolved by deletion after re-reading the task package's Taskbar section, which defines enablement/font/width/alignment/entry composition but no reset-time mode; the native strip renders no reset text either. Inventing a consumer would have meant changing the taskbar content contract, which is phase 3 (item G) and needs screenshot acceptance. Guard rails: QuotaPercentContext vs QuotaDisplayContext with ResetAwareComponent = floatBar|dashboard makes asking the taskbar for a reset mode a type error, and settings::tests::taskbar_has_no_reset_time_mode_setting asserts the key is never persisted. A same-root bug was fixed alongside: TaskbarTab's preview hardcoded 'Codex 59%' / weekly 18% regardless of taskbarShowAsUsed, so it now runs its sample numbers through the shared percentage layer. P1-2's fix is deliberately broader than the finding: the review cited isInformational, but balance providers (DeepSeek, MiMo) carry prepaid amounts in synthetic 0% windows that are NOT informational-flagged, so an isInformational-only check would still have leaked a 0% bar; primaryQuotaState reuses getProviderBalance().excludeWindows, the same source the cards use. P2 (dashboard covering both the tray flyout and the PopOut panel) was left open for the user rather than decided unilaterally.
